name: Substitution (ibdāl)
definition: Putting one letter in the place of another in a word, for ease of pronunciation, outside the changes of the weak letters: above all the tāʾ of the pattern iftaʿala after certain letters.
body: The best-known case is the pattern iftaʿala. After ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ its tāʾ becomes ṭāʾ (iṣṭabara from ṣ-b-r); after dāl, dhāl and zāy it becomes dāl (izdajara from z-j-r); and a first-letter wāw or yāʾ becomes tāʾ and merges with it (ittaʿada from w-ʿ-d). Ibdāl also names the change of a weak letter to hamza (qāʾil from q-w-l).

The books separate ibdāl from iʿlāl, though they overlap, and list the letters of substitution; Ibn ʿUṣfūr's al-Mumtiʿ and al-Shāfiya treat them in full, and Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Lughawī wrote a book of substituted words.

examples.text: iṣṭabara, from ṣ-b-r on iftaʿala: the tāʾ becomes ṭāʾ after ṣād.
izdajara, from z-j-r: the tāʾ becomes dāl after zāy.
ittaʿada, from w-ʿ-d: the wāw becomes tāʾ and merges with the tāʾ of the pattern.
